Hi Sam — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and a few asks so we can scope the PO and DPA redline.

Summary notes:
- Primary workload: clinical notes ingestion (PII: names, MRNs, free-text PHI) + embeddings for search.
- Expected QPS: ~80 requests/sec for retrieval; peak batch ingest ~20k documents/day.

Can you confirm the following so we can route the right privacy docs to your team?
1) Data residency: must remain in us-east-1 for initial deployment; are there any EU-only constraints for this pilot?
2) Retention: requested 30 days on raw text, 12 months for derived embeddings — is that firm?
3) Logging: you asked that logs redact patient identifiers and keep only request/response metadata for 90 days — confirm acceptable.
4) Breach notification: procurement asked for a 72-hour initial notification SLA and a forensic report within 30 days. Is that your baseline ask?

Attachments: demo recording + architecture diagram (see links below).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share our DPA draft and current subprocessors list for your legal team to review (Marissa looping).
- Marissa / Rishi will confirm retention/residency feasibility and any required contractual language.
- If everything aligns, procurement review planned for 09/23.

Thanks — let me know if I missed anything.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Alex — great demo, thanks. Answers below: 

1) Residency: Pilot needs data stored and processed in US only (us-east-1). No EU residency required for this project.
2) Retention: We prefer 30 days for raw text and 12 months for embeddings — that matches our initial ask. Could you confirm support for a hard retention delete?
3) Logging: We need request/response traces for debugging but PHI must be redacted. 90 days retention for logs is fine.
4) Breach notification: Procurement will expect an initial notification within 72 hours and regular updates; a 30-day forensic report target is acceptable.

I'm attaching our vendor security questionnaire and a short procurement checklist. Procurement lead (Lia Ortiz) will join next thread for contracting.

Thanks,

Alex — thanks for the forward and good clarity from Sam. High-level answers and suggested DPA language below.

Controller vs Processor:
- Redwood acts as a processor for inference and storage when we host and process customer data under the customer account. We can accept processor role language in the DPA and include the specific processing activities (inference, embeddings, ephemeral KV cache).

Residency & Hard Delete:
- We can support tenant-level pinning to us-east-1 for both storage and inference at pilot scale.
- Hard delete: we can implement an automated retention policy to purge raw text after 30 days; we recommend a documented deletion certificate in the DPA (we can provide delete logs).

Logging / Redaction:
- Application logs will be configurable to redact fields identified as PHI; we will keep request/response metadata for 90 days. If Medicore requires end-to-end redaction verification we suggest a short runbook test during onboarding.

Subprocessors & Notice:
- Attached is the current subprocessors export and our DPA draft with the clause we propose for subprocessor engagement and prior notice. We typically provide a 30-day notice for material subprocessor changes.

Breach notification and forensic timeline:
- Redwood's practice: initial notification without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after confirming a security event impacting customer data. We commit to a preliminary incident report and then a forensic/body-of-evidence report as it becomes available; target delivery of a detailed forensic report within 30 days for significant incidents.

Next steps:
- I’m attaching the redwood-dpa-draft.pdf and the subprocessors CSV. Alex — send these directly to Lia and Sam. If procurement wants tighter SLA language we can accept a short amendment to the DPA limited to notification timelines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference
